title: paged-kv-cache: adaptive block allocator + locality-aware reuse & pinning
author: Ava Chen
body:
Motivation: The paged KV cache block manager has been a major source of tail-latency and suboptimal memory reuse under multimodal workloads. We frequently observe fragmentation and cross-stream thrashing when sequence-length distributions vary, and locality-unaware pinning prevents high-reuse hot keys from staying resident efficiently. This PR implements an adaptive block allocator plus locality-aware reuse and pinning heuristics to reduce allocation churn, improve KV cache hit-rate for hot prefixes, and lower tail latency under continuous-batching workloads.

Summary of changes: Implemented a new adaptive block allocator that: 1) tracks allocation size histogram per worker and selects block sizes dynamically to reduce internal fragmentation; 2) groups free blocks by locality buckets to prefer reusing blocks on the same NUMA/GPU memory region; and 3) exposes a lightweight TTL-and-frequency-based pinning policy which keeps frequently-accessed KV blocks resident for a configurable window. Added eviction-preferred flags and a soft-pin API used by the router to mark blocks for longer retention during in-flight rollouts.

Key behavioral changes (high level): - Replaced the fixed-size bucket allocator with an adaptive histogram-based allocator. The allocator picks target block sizes from recent allocation patterns and promotes reuse of same-sized blocks. - Locality buckets are keyed by device-id and a coarse memory-region id so reuse prefers same-device blocks when available. This reduces cross-device transfers on pin/unpin cycles for private deployment and dedicated GPU pools. - Soft pinning: blocks receive a soft-pin score (freq * exp(-age/ttl)). Router can bump score on consecutive requests for the same prefix; background sweeper evicts lowest scores first. - Stats and tracing: added metrics for allocation attempts/fallbacks, pin hit-rate, reuse-hit-rate, fragmentation ratio, and per-device median allocation latency. Added structured spans for block allocation hot paths.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks (local perf-lab, p3-standard): - Context: mixed seq-len workload (128,512,2048) with continuous batching at 1200 req/s. - Median token latency: -6.8% (from 12.1ms -> 11.28ms). - 95th percentile token latency: -18.5% (from 32.4ms -> 26.4ms). - KV cache hit-rate increased from 72.3% -> 85.7% on hot prefixes. - Allocator-induced CPU-side GC cycles down by ~40%. End-to-end production canary (10% traffic) on dedicated pool: - P95 generation latency improved ~12%, and incident-side effects (OOM spikes during traffic bursts) did not occur during 48h soak.

Compatibility and rollback: The allocator is behind a feature flag (kv.paged_adaptive_allocator). Soft pin TTL defaults to 30s and can be tuned per-tenant via config. Rollback is safe: when flag is off we revert to legacy allocator; sweeper uses conservative limits so global memory pressure won't exceed configured pool sizes.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for allocator heuristics, integration tests simulating mixed sequence workloads, and end-to-end canary scripts. CI matrix included linux/gcc, macos, and linux-clang. All checks passed after one flaky test fixed (see comments).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-4821 - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Benchmarks captured and attached - [x] Rollout plan + feature flag - [x] Observability (metrics + traces)

Notes for reviewers: Focus on allocator fallback correctness, pinning score compute, and potential contention in the free-list per locality-bucket. I added comments where locking choices were deliberate to minimize fast-path overhead.

Related: builds on prior work in kp: pr-46230/48765 and integrates locality ideas from pr-44890.

review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Could we avoid a global lock by sharding the free lists per locality? I worry about contention at 2k concurrent requests.
Ava Chen (author): Sharded free-lists are used; locality buckets already map to per-shard lists. Added comments and a test to exercise concurrent allocate/free paths.
Priya Iyer: Pin score math looks reasonable, but can we expose a safety cap so a noisy prefix doesn't starve others?
Ava Chen (author): Added a per-tenant pin budget and a decay multiplier; documented defaults in kv_defaults.yaml.
Liam O'Neill: CI flaky test fixed by increasing test harness timeout, ok to merge after perf numbers are validated in canary.
Ava Chen (author): Verified canary metrics and uploaded raw benchmark logs to the ENG-4821 linear thread.
release_notes: Improves paged KV cache allocator with adaptive sizing, locality-aware reuse, and TTL-based pinning; reduces tail latency and increases KV hit-rate. Feature gated behind kv.paged_adaptive_allocator.
